claim: Spike-specific CD4+ T cells from convalescent donors harbored a highly significantly elevated proportion of CXCR4+ CD69+ cells compared to infection-naïve donors
source: Interestingly, spike-specific CD4+ T cells from convalescent donors harbored a highly significantly elevated proportion of CXCR4+ CD69+ cells (Figure 6D), suggesting a potentially superior ability to migrate into pulmonary tissues.

claim: CCR7+ CD62L+ cells were enriched among the spike-specific CD4+ T cells from the convalescent donors compared to infection-naïve donors

evidence: This is supported by the study's experimental data and Figure 6E

claim: After the second vaccine dose, the percentages of CCR7+ CD62L+ spike-specific cells increased as the percentages of spike-specific CD4+ T cells decreased

evidence: This is supported by the study's experimental data and Figure 6F

claim: The expression levels of CCR7 and CD62L on spike-specific CD4+ T cells inversely correlated with the magnitude of the spike-specific CD4+ T cell response
source: This was further supported by our finding that the expression levels of CCR7 and CD62L on spike-specific CD4+ T cells inversely correlated with the magnitude of the spike-specific CD4+ T cell response (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by the study's experimental data and Figure 6G

claim: There was a marked enrichment of both CCR7+ CD62L+ and CXCR4+ CD69+ CD4+ T cells in intranasal specimens compared to blood
source: There was a marked enrichment of both CCR7+ CD62L + and CXCR4+ CD69+ CD4+ T cells in the intranasal specimens (Figure 6H), suggesting that CD4+ T cells expressing these markers preferentially exit the blood and enter the nasopharynx.

claim: Spike-specific CD8+ T cells stimulated by the three different spike proteins (ancestral, B.1.1.7, B.1.351) did not differ in their phenotypic features

claim: All vaccines deployed in areas where the B.1.1.7 or B.1.351 strains dominate have protected vaccinees from severe and fatal COVID-19
source: Although limited data are available, thus far all vaccines deployed in areas where the B.1.1.7 or B.1.351 strains dominate have protected vaccinees from severe and fatal COVID-19 Gupta, 2021.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gupta, 2021

claim: In South Africa where B.1.351 is dominant, the AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 vaccine only prevented ~10% of mild-to-moderate disease cases
source: For example, in South Africa where B.1.351 is dominant, the AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 vaccine only prevented ~10 % of mild-to-moderate disease cases Madhi et al., 2021, while more recent data from Pfizer/BioNTech's vaccine administered in Qatar, where both B.1.1.7 and B.1.351 are dominant, revealed that fully vaccinated individuals were 75 % less likely to develop COVID-19 Abu-Raddad et al., 2021.

evidence: This is supported by citation to Abu-Raddad et al., 2021

claim: The spike-specific antibody response in convalescent individuals after the first mRNA dose is already equivalent to that of infection-naïve individuals after their second mRNA dose
source: Longitudinal serological studies suggest that the spike-specific antibody response in convalescent individuals after the first mRNA dose is already equivalent to that of infection-naïve individuals after their second mRNA dose Goel et al., 2021; Ebinger et al., 2021, suggesting that convalescent individuals may only need a single dose of vaccination.

claim: CD127 expression on SARS-CoV-2-specific T cells has been implicated in COVID-19 disease amelioration

evidence: This is a statement about prior findings

claim: CD127 expression was more frequent on spike-specific CD4+ T cells from ICU patients who eventually survived severe COVID-19 than in those that did not

claim: IL7 can drive homeostatic proliferation and expansion of spike-specific CD4+ T cells
